title: fix network systemd unit state after network prune
body:
## Description

fixes: #29369

 Before, `podman network prune` removed the network without stopping the related Quadlet systemd unit.
This change stops the unit before removing the network, so it becomes inactive after the prune and the network can be created again when needed.

comments.body: [NON-BLOCKING] Packit jobs failed. @podman-container-tools/packit-jobs please check. Everyone else, feel free to ignore.

I have to say I'm not a fan of this change to begin with. If the users work with Quadlet, they should manage the networks via systemd. Prune is just one case of the user pulling things underneath the management layer. 

It's like having a OneShot systemd unit that mounts a volume and expect its status to change because the user manually unmounted the volume.

But, if the team thinks it makes sense, I won't block it
